Chapter 8: Sustaining Momentum—Avoiding Burnout and Cultivating Resilience
As you dig deeper into this work, you might notice it’s easy to start feeling tired, discouraged, or even overwhelmed. The truth is, the scale of injustice out there can seem pretty daunting, and real change rarely happens overnight. So, how do you keep your energy, your hope, and your commitment alive for the long haul?
Here’s what’s important: antiracist practice isn’t a sprint—it’s a marathon. Think about athletes for a second. They need rest, nourishment, and support to keep going strong. The same goes for anyone working toward social change. Burnout? Yeah, it’s a real risk—especially if you’re just starting out or if you’re trying to take on everything at once.
So, how do you actually sustain your momentum? Let’s look at a few practices that can make all the difference.
Pace yourself. Set goals that are realistic. Remember, big change takes time, and that’s okay.
Celebrate progress. Take a moment to appreciate those small wins—whether they’re personal breakthroughs or victories you share with others.
Seek community. Connect with people who share your values. When you lean on each other, you share both the struggles and the encouragement.
Practice self-care. Stay in tune with your emotional, physical, and spiritual needs. When you take care of yourself, you’re much better equipped to show up for others.
Stay connected to your purpose. Remind yourself why you started this journey, and picture the kind of world you want to help create.
Let me give you a real-world example. Imagine someone who’s poured themselves into activism for a while, only to end up feeling totally exhausted and maybe even a little disillusioned. Instead of dropping out for good, they decide to pause, rest, and reach out to friends who really get it. After some honest reflection and support, they come back to the work—this time with fresh energy and a clearer perspective.
Here’s the key: resilience isn’t about never getting tired or discouraged. It’s about learning how to recover, adapt, and keep moving forward. When you take care of yourself—and support each other—you make it possible to do this work, not just for a moment, but for the long term.
